source.title: World Modeling in Transformers
source.authors: P. Beckmann; Matthieu Queloz; André Freitas

record.tranche_reason: The study directly measures overlapping feature directions and tests their interference, but uses mechanistic analyses of TaxiGPT rather than the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The study reports superposition geometry, affordance organization, and interventions on position representations that affect illegal-move predictions. It also reports many world-modeling results unrelated to the claim; those are not included.
record.test_reason: In GPT-2-style transformers trained on synthetic Manhattan navigation, the study measures the geometry of 4,516 intersection feature directions: a compressed subspace and above-random overlap. It is a new setting (not toy models, not natural-language LLMs) with its own result on whether trained transformers store more features than dimensions as overlapping directions. The interference and affordance-packing results measure related constructs that no version names.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors' main claim is that TaxiGPT has a faithful, causally used internal map. They attribute its behavioral failures to localization errors from interference between superposed intersection features, not to an incoherent map. Affordance packing mitigates those errors. Better models show less superposed position codes.
record.recipe_differences: Uses diff-means features, probes, representation geometry, and causal interventions in TaxiGPT rather than the original toy-model setup and method.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature geometry and affordance organization differ across the compared datasets, architectures, and training objectives.

fits_no_version.finding: Superposed intersection features are packed by affordance. 91.4% of features are nearest their own legal-move group mean. Clustering aligns with affordance (AMI .574) more than with geography (.192).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Trained transformers pack superposed features by functional similarity (shared downstream effects), limiting the cost of interference.

fits_no_version.finding: Weak position writes plus noise let a wrong superposed feature dominate and cause illegal moves. Repairs remove 55–80% of illegal probability in fatal slips (random-direction controls shown). Steering toward a wrong node yields illegal moves in 18–48% of cases, against 12% for a random direction.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Interference between superposed features causes behavioral errors out of distribution in trained transformers.

record.problems: The study does not vary feature sparsity or importance, so it cannot establish the proposed dependence on either. Its geometry and interference results concern a synthetic navigation task, and some plotted intervention values are not numerically stated in the text.
record.rows_left_out: Other world-modeling measurements and behavioral tests were omitted where they do not measure feature overlap, affordance geometry, or its interference effects.

untested.parts: All of it. No small toy network, no variation of sparsity or importance, no phase transition, no polytope geometry.
All of it. No neuron-level polysemanticity and no test of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
Natural-language LLMs, spreading across neurons, and SAE recovery. Only residual-stream diff-means directions in synthetic-task transformers are measured.
All of it. An SAE is mentioned only as exploratory motivation for the compass.
Not compared. The study uses 1-D intersection directions, but the goal compass is a 2-D circular feature, and the two are not contrasted as units of superposition.

missing.what: Participation ratio of 101 for the layer-18 features; nearest feature shares affordance 61.0%.
Through training, d90 grows from 1 to 204 dims and nearest-neighbor angle from 4.4° to 46.4°. Authors state better models show less superposed features.
Write strength is weaker when the current feature overlaps with many others (crowding, cos>0.5).

record.verdict_notes: Not linked to V1: the systems are 12–48 layer trained transformers, not small toy networks. The 'superposition' here is of mutually exclusive class centroids extracted by diff-means, so compression into a subspace partly follows from the extraction method. The above-random overlap (.073 vs .020) is the more direct evidence. Rows R9–R16 measure interference effects rather than any version's behaviour, and are moved to fits_no_version.

versions.untested_parts: Does not vary feature sparsity or importance, measure a sparsity-dependent transition, or test the original toy-model setup. It studies intersection representations in TaxiGPT.
Does not test neuron polysemanticity, whether important features receive dedicated dimensions, or whether other features share capacity.
Does not test whether polysemantic neurons arise for reasons other than capacity pressure.
Tests feature directions in TaxiGPT models trained on a synthetic navigation task, not general-purpose LLMs broadly; does not test SAE recovery.
Does not test whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.
Uses direction-based intersection features but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional features.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Measured the subspace occupied by layer-18 intersection directions.
rows.measure: Dimensions accounting for 90% of feature variance
rows.note: The model has more measured intersection directions than residual-stream dimensions.
rows.check: Not linked to V1: a 48-layer GPT2-XL is not a small toy network. Baseline should state that the space is 1,600-dimensional and holds 4,516 directions. The directions are diff-means class centroids of mutually exclusive positions, so low-dimensional occupancy is partly built into the extraction method.

source_check.correct: 244 dimensions explain 90% of variance among 4,516 intersection directions at layer 18 in the 1,600-dimensional residual stream. Link to none; state cannot_determine for V4's LLM claim.
source_check.problem: The measurement is correct, but synthetic-navigation transformers do not establish V4's claim about LLMs.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Measured cosine overlap among layer-18 intersection directions.
rows.measure: Mean absolute pairwise cosine; mean nearest-neighbor cosine and angle
rows.baseline: Random directions in the same 1,600-dimensional space: mean absolute cosine .020
rows.value: Feature directions: mean absolute cosine .073; mean nearest-neighbor cosine .668; nearest-neighbor angle 48.1°
rows.note: Directions overlap more than random directions, while the mean nearest neighbor is substantially aligned rather than nearly orthogonal.
rows.check: Unlinked from V1 (system kind). Mean |cos| is .073 against .020 for random directions, so overlap is above random. The nearest-neighbor cosine of .668 means local geometry is not nearly orthogonal.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Measured off-graph moves during the stress test.
rows.note: The paper attributes these failures to weak position writes and noise interacting with superposed intersection features.
rows.check: This is a behavioral failure rate, not a measure of superposition. Attributing it to interference is the authors' interpretation.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL
rows.operation_detail: Weakened the position write and added noise to correctly localized states.

conditions.value: 700 stress rides with initially legal top moves; depth ≥ 60
write caps 300, 240, 200, or 150; noise standard deviations 0, 30, 67, or 120

rows.note: The text states that weakening the write and adding noise causally reproduce off-graph moves; plotted rates are not transcribed here.
rows.check: This is an induced write-cap and noise intervention on interference; no version names it. Values are figure only.

rows.subject: GPT2-XL

rows.measure: Fraction of illegal-move probability mass removed
rows.note: The paper reports this among three repairs that significantly reduce illegal probability mass.
rows.check: This is an interference repair on fatal slips (25% of failures), not a version measure. The baseline is random-direction edits of matched norm (Fig. 5 gray marks).

relationships.condition: GPT-2-style transformers (384d–1,600d) trained on synthetic Manhattan navigation
relationships.reason: In all five models, thousands of intersection directions occupy compressed subspaces: 244/1,600 dims in large RW, 162–251 dims elsewhere. Mean |cos| .073 exceeds the .020 random baseline (R1, R2, R5–R8). These are synthetic-task transformers, not language LLMs, and SP/NSP features decode poorly.
relationships.display_finding: In all five models, thousands of intersection directions occupied compressed subspaces (244 of 1,600 dims in the large RW model, 162–251 elsewhere), with mean |cos| 0.073 against a 0.020 random baseline. These are transformers trained on synthetic navigation, not language models, and SP/NSP features decoded poorly.
